title: Queen of Wands Tarot Card Meaning: Upright, Reversed & Love
description: Queen of Wands upright: confidence, warmth, charisma; reversed: self-doubt, jealousy. Love, work, advice and Waite's 1911 text. Draw it for your question.
h1: Queen of Wands Tarot Card Meaning
image_alt: Queen of Wands, 1909 Rider–Waite–Smith card: a crowned queen in yellow on a lion throne holds a leafy wand and a sunflower, a black cat at her feet.
capsule: The Queen of Wands stands for confidence, warmth and charisma, the independence of someone happy to be seen. Reversed, that fire can dim into self-doubt or flare into jealousy. A bright card overall; her shadow is giving out so much heat that none is left for you. For yes or no, she answers yes, seated relaxed among her lions.

blocks.heading: What is on the Queen of Wands card?
paragraphs: A queen sits facing us on a throne with carved lion heads on its arms, a tall leafy wand in one hand and a sunflower in the other. Waite's note for this card is short: the wands of this suit "are always in leaf, as it is a suit of life and animation" (p. 172). He adds that the Queen's personality matches the King's "but is more magnetic" (p. 172).

On the 1909 card she wears a yellow robe under a white cloak and a crown wreathed in green leaves. Two red lions stand upright on the tall back of the throne among painted sunflowers, yellow pyramid shapes rise at the far left, and a black cat sits right in front of her feet, looking out at us. Waite's note (p. 172) says nothing about the cat or the sunflower, so they are described here, not explained.

blocks.heading: What did Waite write about the Queen of Wands?
paragraphs: Waite's Queen is a friendly, loving, honorable countrywoman with a practical streak, since he also gives her love of money and some success in business (p. 172). His reversed list stays kind and thrifty, though Waite notes that next to certain cards it can mean "opposition, jealousy, even deceit and infidelity" (p. 172).
In his extra list Waite calls her "a good harvest, which may be taken in several senses" (p. 288).

blocks.heading: What does the Queen of Wands mean upright?
paragraphs: Sunflower in one hand, wand in the other, the Queen of Wands is confidence that does not need to shout. She stands for warmth, charisma and independence: a person who knows what they want, says it in their own voice and draws others in simply by being fully themselves. She is also linked with courage, social ease and a full, busy life.

When she turns up, the question is whether you are taking up the space that is yours. Speak first in the meeting, show the work, wear the bright color. Confidence like hers tends to spread, and the people around you can borrow some of it.

blocks.heading: What does the Queen of Wands mean reversed?
paragraphs: Reversed, the Queen of Wands can describe a dimmed light: self-doubt, staying small to avoid attention, or warmth that has turned into impatience because you feel overstretched. Jealousy and comparison belong to this side as well, the sense that someone else is shining in your place. Jealousy is in Waite's reversed list too (p. 172); the self-doubt and the dimmed light are a modern reading, not Waite's.
The way back is small and concrete. Do one thing that makes you feel like yourself again where others can see it, and hand one task back so your fire is not spent entirely on everyone else.

blocks.heading: What does the Queen of Wands mean in love?
paragraphs: Warm, direct and openly affectionate: that is how this Queen loves. With a partner, she brings back flirting, honesty about desire and the nerve to ask for what you want without shrinking it. Unattached, you may find her describing a magnetic, sociable time in which you meet people as yourself, not as a version built to please.

Upside down, she shows jealousy, insecurity, or warmth given to earn approval. Give from confidence, not from the need to be chosen, and let attraction be something you enjoy rather than something you audition for.

blocks.heading: What does the Queen of Wands mean for work and money?
paragraphs: Few cards suit a public role better: leading a team, selling an idea, running your own project, being the face of something. The Queen brings drive, people skills and the stamina to see things through; reversed, she can mean doing everyone's job at once until the spark goes out.

For money, the card means confident earning: income from your own initiative, a business with your name on it, ease in asking to be paid what you are worth. Reversed, it describes money stress that comes from spreading yourself too thin.

blocks.heading: What is the advice of the Queen of Wands?
paragraphs: Wear, say or do one thing that makes you feel fully yourself, and do it where it can be seen. Then notice who receives most of your energy, and keep some of that warmth for your own plans.

blocks.heading: Is the Queen of Wands a yes or no card?
The Queen of Wands as a person and as feelings
paragraphs: Taken as a person, the Queen of Wands is confident, sociable and warm, with a strong will and a calendar full of projects; she can be anyone, including you on a day you feel sure of yourself. As feelings, she stands for admiration and warm, passionate interest: attraction to someone's confidence, enthusiasm shown openly rather than hidden. Reversed, the same feelings tip into jealousy, insecurity or a possessive streak, or the warmth cools because too much else claims the energy.

blocks.heading: The Queen of Wands with other cards

pairs.text: Two bright cards together: confidence and joy, a moment to be seen and to enjoy it.
Warmth among friends; a sociable, celebrating time with you near the center.
Confidence that earns recognition. Accept the praise without making it smaller.
Too much carried by one person, so the Queen's warmth is spread thin. Hand something back.

blocks.heading: Queen of Wands, Strength or Queen of Pentacles?
paragraphs: Strength also pairs a woman with a lion, but Waite's figure "is closing the jaws of a lion" (p. 100), and that card is read as patience and gentle inner courage. The Queen of Wands rules beside her lions; her card is outward confidence and drive, not quiet taming.

Waite writes that the Queen of Pentacles "contemplates her symbol and may see worlds therein" (p. 256); today she means practical care and a secure home. Both queens are generous, but Pentacles builds comfort while Wands spreads energy.

blocks.heading: Questions to ask yourself about the Queen of Wands
paragraphs: Where am I making myself smaller than I am?
Who or what is using up the warmth I need for myself?
What would I do next if I fully trusted my own voice?

faq.q: Is the Queen of Wands a good or bad card?
faq.a: Good. She brings confidence, warmth and the nerve to be visible, which helps in love, work and friendship alike. Her harder side, jealousy or a spark gone quiet, appears mostly when she is upside down, and even then it names something you can change.

faq.q: Does the Queen of Wands represent a woman?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Waite opens her list with "a dark woman, countrywoman, friendly" (p. 172), yet on Arcana Diary the Queen is a role open to anyone of any gender, including you, whenever her sunny, self-assured energy is the theme.

faq.q: What does the black cat on the Queen of Wands mean?
faq.a: Waite gives it no meaning at all: his notes on this Queen (p. 172) mention only the leafy wands and her magnetic personality, so the cat stays part of the picture without an explanation from him, and this page does not invent one. The animal, like the sunflower, is simply there to be seen.

waite.quote: A dark woman, countrywoman, friendly, chaste, loving, honourable … Also, love of money, or a certain success in business. Reversed: Good, economical, obliging, serviceable.
